subject: Dedicated GPU pools technical breakout — timing and agenda
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: FinWave Platform Team <platform@finwave.io>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Deep-dive on dedicated GPU pool sizing & isolation

Hi Kimberly / Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our infra and platform teams at FinWave would like a focused technical breakout with Redwood to validate sizing assumptions and isolation strategies before our pilot. High-level goals:

- Confirm pool sizing for our steady/peak workload mix (mixed short/long-context requests)
- Validate autoscaling triggers and warm/cold startup latency expectations
- Review tenant isolation patterns and failure domains (VM / container / GPU isolation)
- Discuss failover and cross-region fallback for priority traffic

Would your team be available for a 60–90 minute session the week of Feb 24? We can do any of the following windows (Pacific time):
- Wed Feb 24: 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00
- Thu Feb 25: 09:00–11:00 or 15:00–17:00
- Fri Feb 26: 11:00–13:00

Attendees on our side will be me, Oscar (platform lead), and one SRE. Please let me know who you suggest from Redwood and an agenda — we want to be efficient. Attached is a short infra summary (FinWave-infra.pdf) to give context.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, FinWave Inc.

--
Attachment: FinWave-infra.pdf (summary)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finwave.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deep-dive on dedicated GPU pool sizing & isolation

Hi Samira — great to hear from you and thanks for the summary. We can absolutely run a targeted technical breakout. Suggested approach: 90 min session with the following agenda:

1) 5 min — Introductions & objectives
2) 25 min — FinWave workload profile + constraints (you)
3) 30 min — Redwood recommended pool topologies, steady vs. burst sizing, and cost tradeoffs
4) 15 min — Autoscale policies and cold start mitigation (queueing, warm pools, KV cache priming)
5) 15 min — Isolation & failure domain patterns (multi-tenant isolates, per-customer pools, network and KMS considerations)
6) 5 min — Next steps / action items

We can cover failover briefly; if you want deeper DR we can follow with a focused follow-up.

For times, we can do:
- Thu Feb 25, 09:00–10:30 PT
- Wed Feb 24, 14:00–15:30 PT

Please confirm which slot works for you. I'll invite ML infra (Sergio), capacity engineering (Marcus), and product (Laura) to join — sound good? Zoom link and an invite will follow once we lock time.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

--
Note: attaching a short runbook skeleton in the follow-up.

- Sample QPS / request size distribution (tokens, mean/95th latency)
- Current cold-start numbers and accepted SLA
- Any constraints on egress or KMS that require advance planning

Appreciate it,
Samira

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deep-dive on dedicated GPU pool sizing & isolation — schedule update

Hi Samira — we can move the start 30 minutes earlier and run 13:30–15:00 PT on Wed Feb 24. I've tentatively created a calendar invite (calendar-invite.ics) and added the Zoom link.

Prep notes for the Redwood attendees (short):
- Please bring: current token/sec estimates, 95th latency requirements to inform batching/queue sizing.
- We'll present two pool topologies: (A) shared multi-tenant pools with soft isolation (workload classing + namespaces) and (B) per-customer pinned pools (dedicated schedulers). We'll show cost/latency tradeoffs with sample numbers.
- Autoscale will be discussed with rules: CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, queue depth, and pre-warming windows (we'll share a recommendation doc).
- Security touches: Laura will outline KMS boundaries and audit log requirements; Sergio will cover tenant blast radius controls.

Attached is an early runbook skeleton for the session (runbook-draft.md) — please review and add items. If FinWave can provide the QPS / token distribution beforehand (one pager), that will let us prepare concrete sizing examples.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
